doc.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013

title: The Ed Sullivan ad hoc band and aftermath
summary: The messy Sullivan Show performance by Mingus, Shepp and Rahsaan, and later friendly ties with Andy Cyrille.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Well there were a bunch of people who were involved in this who were not necessarily on this same page musically. But they put together an ad hoc band that included Mingus, Archie, Rahsann and I forget who the drummer was, somebody else. And what they played was — even for somebody like me who is familiar with what was then called avante garde jazz — it was a total mess. And for anything, to try to appeal to the broad mass of listeners. It’s just — they should have played a tune. They played a song that people were familiar with, God, it wouldn’t have been anything that they had to be ashamed of to try to play something that made musical sense, but it was totally, totally © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-

out there. So the whole thing was a total flop. And it was childish. And later on Andy, who is still very much around — so is Archie but I hardly ever see him, he isn’t playing anymore. He had trouble with his embouchure too. But Andy has been to the Institute quite a few times and we’ve become friendly. That’s all over, all that stuff. And Rahsann, who was a really — you know he was a terrific person but he was being used by these people. Well anyway that’s all over, that’s long — water under the bridge and we don’t really have any of that stuff going on anymore. But there are still occasions when something will come up and there are still people who feel that – until this day -- there are things that are wrong in the so-called music business and that black artists are still being taken advantage of and that they’re still — and it comes up once in a while.
